item.title: Buddhist monk arrested in Thailand on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m
item.description: Phra Wachirayan Wi arrested alongside woman he was filmed having sex with in latest scandal to hit country’s clergy Police in Thailand have arrested a senior Buddhist monk on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m intended for his monastery, alongside a suspected female accomplice he was filmed having sex with. The case is the latest scandal to hit the clergy in the Buddhist-majority country, after a sex and extortion case involving senior monks last year prompted public outrage and calls for greater scrutiny of temple finances. item.title: No pit stops: Chinese coal mine makes big upgrade with autonomous electric trucks
item.description: In north China’s Inner Mongolia autonomous region, home to the country’s largest coal reserves, a vast open-pit mine cuts deep into the earth, shrouded in clouds of dust. Winters here are long and brutal, with temperatures plunging to as low as minus 40 degrees Celsius (minus 40 degrees Fahrenheit). In older, more traditional days, hundreds of truck drivers, bundled in heavy winter gear, had to brave icy roads and the risk of frostbite as they hauled loads through the pit. When dense fog and... item.title: Zhang Ziyu: la gigante china que revoluciona el baloncesto femenino
item.description: Con 19 años y 2,23 metros de altura, Zhang Ziyu se ha convertido en una de las grandes protagonistas del Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto en Alemania. La pívot de la selección china, considerada la jugadora más alta de la historia del baloncesto profesional femenino, ha irrumpido con fuerza en la escena internacional. Pero su entrenador apuesta por una integración progresiva mientras la joven gigante se adapta a las exigencias de la élite. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Builders hauled 25-ton stones 11 miles to create the ‘Devil’s Arrows’
item.description: Recent studies indicate that the Neolithic builders of the Devil's Arrows transported massive 25-tonne stones from Brimham Rocks, located 18 kilometers away, rather than using nearby glacial deposits. This geological research has resolved a persistent mystery regarding the stones' lineage. Additionally, a previously unaccounted for stone has been traced to a medieval cross found in Aldborough village, reinforcing local folklore about their historical significance. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: REPLAY: Hegseth warns of 'Islamist threat' at 9/11 25th anniversary commemorations
item.description: US defense secretary Pete Hegseth delivered remarks at a ceremony at the Pentagon on Friday on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks. Hegseth used his speech to turn to the ongoing conflict in Iran and sought to connect it to the 2001 attacks on America. ““Our warriors have fought an Islamic theocracy that has wished us death for nearly half a century, that cheered on 9/11, a regime that has sponsored terrorist attacks against Americans for decades, killing thousands, including our comrades in Iraq, in Afghanistan," he said. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Tierras raras en Brasil: ¿una oportunidad o una amenaza ambiental?
item.description: Brasil avanza hacia una mayor regulación de la exploración de sus tierras raras, unos minerales estratégicos para la transición energética, la industria tecnológica y el sector militar. El país cuenta con algunas de las mayores reservas del mundo, pero gran parte de estos recursos permanece todavía bajo tierra, mientras China domina la producción global. La apuesta brasileña abre una nueva disputa por estos minerales, pero también despierta preocupación entre comunidades indígenas por el posible impacto ambiental de su explotación. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Hate speech against Rohingya refugees on the rise in Malaysia
item.description: Hostile social media content, disinformation campaigns, and a petition calling for their expulsion: in Malaysia, a wave of hate speech has been targeting Rohingya refugees, a Muslim minority driven out of Myanmar. The rising hostility has already led to the eviction of more than 100 people from a village and forced the temporary closure of schools serving refugee children. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: The creator of a sculpture commemorating those killed in the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown will ask Danish authorities to negotiate with Hong Kong for its return, with city officials disputing his claims of owning the confiscated artwork. The fate of the “Pillar of Shame” sculpture has come back under the spotlight after the High Court on Friday handed jail sentences to three former leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China at the end of a... item.title: 25 years after 9/11, al Qaeda remains a threat – even as Washington looks away
item.description: A quarter of a century after the deadliest terrorist attacks in US history, al Qaeda’s various branches have moved away from the global jihad advocated by Osama bin Laden, focusing instead on regional insurgencies. Their actions continue to destabilise swathes of the world, from the Sahel to Afghanistan, neglected by a US administration that critics say has unlearned the lessons of 9/11. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: Construction has officially begun on the last commercial office tower at the World Trade Center site. This impressive 55-story structure will be the new global headquarters for American Express. Spanning nearly two million square feet, it’s projected to be fully operational by 2031, contributing billions to the economy and creating thousands of new jobs. This marks a pivotal milestone in the site's redevelopment after 25 years. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: US consumer prices accelerated in August as the cost of petrol rebounded after two straight monthly declines, bolstering financial market expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates next week. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 0.4 per cent last month after edging up 0.1 per cent in July, the Labour Department’s Bureau of Labour Statistics ‌said on Friday. item.title: Study reveals link between Tibetan Plateau heat and record rain in California
item.description: Abnormally high temperatures across the Tibetan Plateau in early winter can trigger catastrophic rainstorms in California, according to a new study revealing a previously unidentified climate connection. In the winters of 2016-2017 and 2022-2023, record-breaking rain swept across the US state and surrounding areas, causing billions of dollars in damage and several deaths during years when drier weather was expected in the region. A study led by researchers from the University of California, Los... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Scientists fitted GPS collars to 17 lions and 14 hyenas expecting hyenas to follow lions
item.description: A groundbreaking study suggests that it's the male lions that approach spotted hyenas, contrary to the belief that hyenas seek out lion remains for food. In fact, spotted hyenas are known to back away from lions, prioritizing their safety. This finding highlights the importance of spatial avoidance in hyena behavior, emphasizing their adaptive strategies to circumvent confrontations with such powerful hunters. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A new surface atlas of Phobos will help MMX mission collect its samples
item.description: Thanks to JAXA, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, and its sample-return capabilities, we're on the cusp of receiving our first sample from the Martian system—not from Mars itself, but from its largest moon, Phobos. JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch in October. It will reach Phobos in 2027 and, if successful, return a sample from the moon to Earth in 2031. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Instead of managing billions, Warren Buffett’s son Howard Buffett chose farming
item.description: Choosing a path less traveled, Howard Buffett, the son of Warren Buffett, dedicated his life to farming and conservation rather than finance. He skillfully managed farms in Nebraska and Illinois, prioritizing soil health. Warren Buffett supported his passion by purchasing a Nebraska farm for his son. As he transitions to the role of non-executive chairman at Berkshire Hathaway, Howard aims to safeguard the company’s culture following his father's legacy. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: US court rules 150,000 Mississippi residents have no constitutional right to lead-free water
item.description: A federal appeals court has determined that the US Constitution does not explicitly provide a right to clean drinking water. Residents of Jackson residents claimed their city was aware of unsafe water conditions but chose to mislead them. Although the court acknowledged the severity of these claims, it denied the establishment of a constitutional right to safe water and pointed to different legal recourses. item.title: After husband’s death, she ensured their 215 acres stay protected
item.description: Becky Shelton made a conscious decision to prioritize land preservation over lucrative offers from developers. By securing her properties in King George and Stafford with legal protections, she ensures these areas remain untouched for future custodians. Shelton views her role as a temporary steward of the earth, taking action to prevent the encroachment of subdivisions and data centers on the natural landscape. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Montana seals 20 hazards at five abandoned uranium sites that once supplied US defence program
item.description: Several abandoned uranium mine sites in Montana’s Pryor Mountains have been closed after assessments found physical hazards, radiation and chemical contamination risks. The project addressed 20 mine features across five historic sites, while also protecting bat habitat, rare plants and cultural resources. Officials said continued monitoring will be needed because erosion, gravity and vandalism can affect mine closures over time. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
